title: In This Town, The Fog Steals What You Hold

publish.title: The FOG Steals Whatever You're Holding In This Town #shorts
publish.description: In this town, when the fog rolls in, whatever is in your hands disappears, until one kid follows it to find out where everything goes. What would you never let go of?
publish.caption: In this town, the fog steals whatever you're holding 🌫️🏆

scenes.line: In this town, the fog *steals* whatever you are holding.
scenes.title: IN THIS TOWN...

scenes.line: It rolls in every Friday. You drop everything and *wait*.
Jay forgot once. He was holding a *sandwich*.
One second later, *gone*. He cried for a week.
Phones, hats, ice cream. The fog takes it *all*.
Nobody ever asked *where* it all went.
Then I won the town spelling bee. My first *trophy*.
I carried it everywhere. I *slept* with it.
So when the fog came on Friday, I was still *holding* it.
One blink. My hands were *empty*.
Everyone said forget it. That is just the *rule*.
I did not forget it. I walked *into* the fog.
The deeper I went, the *quieter* it got.
Then I saw it. A mountain of stolen *stuff*.
Phones. Hats. One very old *sandwich*.
And sitting on top, something small and *white*.
It was not a monster. It was a tiny *cloud*.
It hugged my trophy like a teddy *bear*.
I got *angry*. I told it to give everything back.
The little cloud started to *rain*.
Then I noticed. It never took anything *broken*.
Only things people were holding *tight*. Things they loved.
It just wanted to feel what that was *like*.
So I sat down. And I held out my *hand*.
Nobody had ever held the fog *before*.
The next morning, everything was back on our *doorsteps*.
Even the sandwich. Jay ate it. We do not talk about *that*.
The fog still comes every *Friday*.
But now nobody drops anything. We all hold out a *hand*.
And my trophy? I let the little cloud *keep* it.
